11-2D-1. - Purpose.
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT11UNDECO_CH2DIRE_ARTDTRNEDI_11-2D-1PU","Title":"11-2D-1. - Purpose.","Content":"
\n

\n The purpose of the traditional neighborhood districts is to encourage mixed use, compact\n development that is sensitive to the environmental characteristics of the land and\n facilitates the efficient use of services. Vertically integrated residential projects\n are encouraged in all traditional neighborhood districts. A traditional neighborhood\n district diversifies and integrates land uses within close proximity to each other,\n and it provides for the daily recreational and shopping needs of the residents.\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Old town district (O-T). The purpose of the O-T district is to accommodate and encourage further intensification\n of the historical city center in accord with the Meridian Comprehensive Plan. The\n intent of the O-T district is to delineate a centralized activity center and to encourage\n its renewal, revitalization and growth as the public, quasi-public, cultural, financial\n and recreational center of the city. Public and quasi- public uses integrated with\n general business, and medium high to high density residential is encouraged to provide\n the appropriate mix and intensity of activities necessary to establish a truly urban\n city center.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Traditional neighborhood center district (TN-C). The purpose of the TN-C district is to serve as the focal point of a neighborhood\n center, containing retail, commercial, and community services to meet the daily needs\n of community residents within a one- to two-mile radius. A TN-C is pedestrian oriented,\n and it is designed to encourage pedestrian connection with a traditional neighborhood\n residential district. TN-C district uses include small scale retail, restaurants,\n recreational, personal services, public or quasi-public uses, churches, and attached\n and multifamily dwellings.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Traditional neighborhood residential district (TN-R). The purpose of the TN-R district is to provide for a variety of residential land\n uses including attached and detached single-family residential, duplex, townhouse,\n and multifamily. A TN-R district includes open spaces and promotes pedestrian activity\n through well designed and varied streetscapes that also provide for the safe and efficient\n movement of vehicular traffic. Most dwelling units should be accessed from alleys.\n The minimum density is six (6) units per acre. Density should decrease away from the\n center and closer to conventional residential districts. The TN-R district should\n be generally located adjacent to a TN-C district, along a transit corridor, or within\n a mixed-use neighborhood. For the purposes of this title, the term residential district\n shall also include the traditional neighborhood residential district.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n (Ord. 05-1170, 8-30-2005, eff. 9-15-2005; Ord. 16-1717, 1-3-2017)\n
